proverb_bn: পাগলে কী না বলে, ছাগলে কী না খায়
romanised: Pagole ki na bole, chhagole ki na khay.
meaning_en: Don't take the nonsense of foolish people seriously.
conversation:
Mitali: Did you see the comment that man posted under your painting? He says it's the worst thing he's ever seen.
Shyamal: The same man also posted that the earth is flat. Pagole ki na bole, chhagole ki na khay.
correct: Shyamal won't take the man's insult seriously because the man talks nonsense.
literal: Mad people will say all sorts of things, and goats will eat all sorts of things.
plausible: Shyamal is hurt by the comment and is thinking of giving up painting.

meaning_en: Fake sympathy from someone who doesn't really care.
conversation:
Nandini: The manager who blocked Ruma's promotion is now telling everyone how sad he is that she resigned.
Subho: Machher mayer putroshok.
correct: The manager's sorrow over Ruma's resignation is fake.
literal: A mother fish is grieving deeply for her lost son.
plausible: The manager truly regrets losing such a good employee as Ruma.

meaning_en: People become obedient only when forced.
conversation:
Bulbul: The landlord ignored our leaking roof for a year, but fixed it the day after we complained to the municipality.
Swarup: Thelar nam babaji.
correct: The landlord only acted once he was put under pressure.
literal: Pressure is given the respectful name of 'revered sir'.
plausible: The landlord fixed it only because he finally had the money for it.

meaning_en: People become obedient only when forced.
conversation:
Sumi: My passport file was stuck for months, but it moved in two days once the newspaper ran a story.
Alamgir: Thelar nam babaji.
correct: The office only worked on the file once public pressure pushed it.
literal: 'Respected father' is the polite name given to a hard push.
plausible: The file was delayed only by an ordinary backlog that has now cleared.

proverb_bn: কাজের বেলায় কাজি, কাজ ফুরোলে পাজি
romanised: Kajer belay kaji, kaj phurole paji.
meaning_en: People value you only while they need you.
conversation:
Sumaiya: Rafi borrowed my notes before every exam, and now that exams are over he ignores me in the corridor.
Nayeem: Kajer belay kaji, kaj phurole paji.
correct: Rafi was friendly only while he needed Sumaiya's notes.
literal: Someone is a qazi at work time and a villain when the work is done.
plausible: Nayeem thinks Rafi is just shy now that the exams are over.

meaning_en: Speaking beyond one's position or experience.
conversation:
Kunal: A first-year student stood up at the seminar and corrected the Nobel laureate's economics.
Afsana: Chhoto mukhe boro kotha.
correct: The student spoke far beyond his standing and experience.
literal: Large, important words came out of the student's very small mouth.
plausible: Afsana thinks the student was right to correct the laureate.

meaning_en: Everyone is guilty; if you remove the dishonest, no one is left.
conversation:
Shohel: The anti-corruption team wants to suspend every officer who has ever taken a bribe at the land office.
Rubina: Thog bachhte ga ujar.
correct: Almost everyone there is corrupt, so nobody would be left.
literal: Weeding out the cheats would leave the whole village empty.
plausible: Rubina thinks only a few junior officers at the land office take bribes.

meaning_en: Two people or things that are too different can't get along.
conversation:
Debosmita: My father is a die-hard Mohun Bagan fan and my father-in-law is East Bengal to the bone. Every family dinner ends in a fight.
Farhan: Tele jole mish khay na.
correct: The two fathers are far too different ever to get along.
literal: Oil and water simply cannot mix, however long you stir them together.
plausible: Farhan thinks the two fathers secretly enjoy their dinner fights.

meaning_en: A bad person always finds an excuse.
conversation:
Sohom: The contractor took the advance and vanished. Now it's the cement shortage, then his mother's illness, then the rain.
Jayita: Durjoner chholer obhab hoy na.
correct: A dishonest man like the contractor always finds an excuse.
literal: The contractor literally keeps a supply of excuses stored away.
plausible: Jayita believes the contractor's mother really is seriously ill this time.

meaning_en: A bad person always finds an excuse.
conversation:
Tamal: My colleague missed the deadline again. First it was the Wi-Fi, now it's a 'family function'.
Raisa: Durjoner chholer obhab hoy na.
correct: Someone like him will always come up with another excuse.
literal: A wicked man never runs short of excuses, as if he keeps a stock of them.
plausible: Raisa thinks the colleague's Wi-Fi really was broken that week.

meaning_en: Keeping quiet keeps you out of trouble.
conversation:
Yasin: At the village shalish, both sides shouted at everyone who spoke. My father said nothing, and both sides still respect him.
Morium: Bobar shotru nei.
correct: Staying silent kept Yasin's father out of trouble with both sides.
literal: A man who is unable to speak makes no enemies on either side of a fight.
plausible: Morium thinks Yasin's father secretly supports one of the two sides.

meaning_en: Someone who is extremely slow at getting things done.
conversation:
Sriparna: I applied for a passport correction in March. The office says 'next week' every single week.
Mehrab: Atharo mashe bochhor.
correct: The passport office is incredibly slow at getting anything done.
literal: At the passport office, a single year lasts for a full eighteen months.
plausible: Mehrab thinks the correction will surely be ready next week.

meaning_en: Hiding one's need out of shyness or pride.
conversation:
Agnibha: At the wedding, the new groom barely touched the food because everyone was watching. He told me later he was starving.
Shabnur: Pete khide mukhe laj.
correct: The groom hid how hungry he was because he felt shy in front of everyone.
literal: The groom's belly was hungry, but his face was full of shyness.
plausible: Shabnur thinks the groom simply didn't like the wedding food.

meaning_en: Wrongdoing always catches up with the wrongdoer.
conversation:
Debojyoti: Ten years ago Ghosh-babu cheated his brother out of the family house. Now his own son has thrown him out of it.
Sanghita: Pap bapkeo chhare na.
correct: Ghosh-babu's wrongdoing has finally caught up with him.
literal: Sin will not even spare the father of the person who committed it.
plausible: Sanghita thinks the son was unfair to throw Ghosh-babu out.

proverb_bn: সাধে কি বাবা বলি, গুঁতোর চোটে বাবা বলি
romanised: Shadhe ki baba boli, gunttor chote baba boli.
meaning_en: Showing respect only because one is forced to.
conversation:
Kibria: Why do you keep praising the union leader on Facebook? You hate him.
Rajon: He decides who gets the overtime. Shadhe ki baba boli, gunttor chote baba boli.
correct: Rajon praises the leader only because he is forced to.
literal: He calls him father not out of love but because of the jabs.
plausible: Rajon has truly come to like the union leader after all this time.

proverb_bn: সাধে কি বাবা বলি, গুঁতোর চোটে বাবা বলি
romanised: Shadhe ki baba boli, gunttor chote baba boli.
meaning_en: Showing respect only because one is forced to.
conversation:
Moyukh: The new director makes us all clap after his boring speeches, and you clap the loudest.
Faria: My appraisal is next month. Shadhe ki baba boli, gunttor chote baba boli.
correct: Faria shows the director respect only because she is under pressure.
literal: She calls him father only because of the jabs, not from love.
plausible: Faria truly enjoys the director's speeches more than anyone.

meaning_en: Wanting something but not being able to afford it.
conversation:
Nurunnabi: Every Eid my son asks for a bicycle, and every Eid I walk past the shop and come home empty-handed.
Sharifa: Shadh achhe shaddho nei.
correct: Nurunnabi wants to buy the bicycle but can't afford it.
literal: He wants to, but he lacks the strength to carry it home.
plausible: Sharifa thinks Nurunnabi doesn't want his son riding on busy roads.

meaning_en: Using what you learned from someone against them.
conversation:
Nirjhar: Sen-babu trained Raju in the sweet-making business for ten years, and now Raju has opened a shop right next door and stolen his customers.
Gitali: Guru mara bidya.
correct: Raju is using what Sen-babu taught him to defeat Sen-babu himself.
literal: Raju learned a skill that is used for killing one's teacher.
plausible: Gitali thinks Sen-babu is happy to see Raju doing so well.
